national.line: A 60-year-old Pennsylvania man broke a Guinness World Record by going to 1,207 movie screenings in one year, about 3.3 movies a day. His popcorn bill must be impressive.
Ariana Grande surprised a runner named Ellie at the New York City Marathon finish line with a kind note she wrote while watching the race. Now that's a medal.
Hundreds of New Jersey students collected over a quarter million pounds of food for food banks, filling the Howell High School football field with groceries. That's a touchdown for hunger.
Kelly Clarkson dressed as Meryl Streep and sang a ghoulish version of the Bee Gees' "Stayin' Alive" for Halloween. Staying in character, she was.

pride.line: Victoria Moroski, a 17-year-old from Lake of the Ozarks, won the under-18 skim world title and Team USA gold at the World Wakesurf Championships in China in October. She's riding high.
pride.label: World Champ

pride.line: Osage Beach pro angler Tyler Williams earned a spot in the 60-angler field for the $1.25 million Champions bass tournament in Tennessee, held Oct. 29 through 31. Fish fear him.
pride.label: Big Tournament

pride.line: Waynesville Career Center welding and manufacturing students built backdrop props for the Tiger Pride Marching Band this fall, saving the band about $10,000. Great work, and a great backdrop.
pride.label: Student Project

pride.line: Ollie Sanders was named Lebanon High School's Yellowjacket of the Week for effort in athletics and the classroom. Favorite moment: winning best colorguard at Carthage. Sounds like a team player.
pride.label: Yellowjacket of the Week

pride.line: Jacob Shurtz of Fair Grove soccer broke the school record for goals in a season, passing his older brother Andrew's 31, and KY3 named him Athlete of the Week. Sibling rivalry, scoreboard edition.
pride.label: School Record

pride.line: Lebanon R-III Schools named Katie Cottongim its new director of communications. Now somebody's in charge of the good news.
pride.label: New Leader

local.line: Chick-fil-A opens in Osage Beach on Thursday, Nov. 5, and customers dressed in cow-themed attire get a free entree. Time to moo-ve fast.
Heritage Bank of the Ozarks was the winning bidder at the Oct. 26 foreclosure sale of Lebanon's Ice Cream Factory property and is working with the city on its future. Let's hope for sprinkles.
Marshfield High School's Marine Corps JROTC program is back after a four-year effort, giving students practical skills, career options and ways to get involved. Mission accomplished.

music.line: Morgan Wallen, Ella Langley and Kings of Leon will headline the 2027 Sand in My Boots Festival in Gulf Shores, Alabama, in May. Pack the sunscreen and the boots.
Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" spent its 26th week at No. 1, extending her own record. That song has a lease on the top.
Zach Top wrapped his Cold Beer & Country Music Tour with a sold-out show at Bridgestone Arena in Nashville. Nothing cold about that finale.
Ella Langley and her band went as Toy Story characters for Halloween after the band and crew voted on a group costume. To infinity and beyond the stage.
Ella Langley loves Halloween, but she told fans to stop throwing candy onstage because it was a tripping hazard. Even stars watch their step.
Morgan Wallen now curates his own 24/7 SiriusXM channel, called Morgan Wallen Radio. Hard to argue with that playlist.
Lainey Wilson's husband, Devlin "Duck" Hodges, says his friends keep asking him to set them up with Ella Langley. Good luck, fellas.
Riley Green says his big dream is still to become a Grand Ole Opry member. The Opry should keep a seat warm.
HARDY and Blake Shelton released a carefree new duet called "Hell." Hot new duet, no pun intended.
Zach Bryan uploaded a new video covering "Kentucky Hurricane" by Ian Noe, a lesser-known Kentucky songwriter. Good taste travels.
Ashley Cooke is releasing her first-ever Christmas EP, called WRAPPED. Early gift for country fans.
Parker McCollum says he's raising his son to be respectful above all else, even if brains don't run in the family. Manners first, math later.

weird.line: Animal rescuers in Virginia solved the mystery of a hawk stuck in a driveway: it was too fat to fly. Even hawks overdo the holidays.
Firefighters in Texas rescued a raccoon spotted high in a tree with its head stuck in a hollow. He's really nosy.
A California officer was lifted to a hangar roof to save a baby raccoon and reunite it with its mom. Best lift of the day.
A Wisconsin angler shattered a decades-old state smallmouth bass record with a 9.7-pound fish caught in Green Bay. Biggest fish story is true.
A Hayward DNR team netted a record 7-foot-4 lake sturgeon in Sawyer County, Wisconsin. That's taller than most basketball players.
A rescued beaver named Blossom showed off his bowling skills at a Mississippi sanctuary, nudging a blue ball and mini pumpkins around. He's a natural.
A black bear on a Craryville, New York, school campus triggered a lockout and a lot of jokes. Class was bear-ly in session.
A Florida man preparing to sell his $500,000 home discovered a $10 quitclaim deed affecting his ownership stake. Read the fine print.
A U.S. student's jet-powered drone hit 491 mph and claimed the world's fastest-flight record for drones. Homework with a boom.
A beaked "hell chicken" dinosaur is the first dinosaur found to have eaten fruit. Even dinosaurs got their five a day.
Rescued bear cubs in Colorado are eating 2,000 pounds of fruit a week because drought wiped out their wild food. That's one big grocery bill.
Sam Trust posted that a friend's wedding gift came presented with a packing slip, calling it the best wedding gift format ever. Gift receipts, level up.
Legend says that if you drive Route 351 near Koppel, Pennsylvania, at night, you might see a glowing green man haunting the highway. Roll up the windows.
Scientists identified one of two 160-million-year-old squid fossils so fat they break every record. Even ancient squid skipped no meals.
Scientists detected dinosaur blood cells in a 115-million-year-old fossil. Talk about a long shelf life.
Honda is trying to break a world record with a 150 mph lawn mower. Mow fast, Saturday chores.

humor.line: Cookie Monster didn't have a name when he first appeared on Sesame Street in 1969, and his appetite covers everything, not just cookies. Me still want cookie.
Deviled eggs are also called eggs mimosa, stuffed eggs and dressed eggs. Same egg, four fancy names.
It started as a day for young kids learning shapes, but anyone can look up, down and every which way for circles. Circle back to this one later.
It marks the first commercial radio broadcast, on Pittsburgh's KDKA in 1920, which happened to be election night. Traffic has been busy ever since.
National Day Calendar started it in 2017 to honor Ohio as the 17th state. Seventeen shows up twice, which is hard to ignore.
It lands on the birthday of John Montagu, the fourth Earl of Sandwich, who by legend came up with the sandwich in 1762. Lunch has been between bread ever since.
It's the one day you're encouraged to use overused phrases as much as possible. Time to hit the ground running.
The idea is to hand someone a dollar and tell them what day it is, so they pass one along too. Cheapest pay-it-forward around.
Jellyfish are about 95 percent water, have no bones, and are not actually fish. Talk about an identity crisis.
A woman who calls herself America's Premier Eventologist created it in 1996, and it lands on every Friday the 13th plus Election Day. Sure, why not.
Howard Carter found King Tut's tomb in 1922, and Tut became pharaoh at age nine. Most nine-year-olds just get a bike.
It's the one day you're officially allowed to ignore everyone who said to go easy on candy. Halloween leftovers, rejoice.
Dr. Marthenia "Tina" Dupree spent twelve years as director of community relations and training at one of the largest chicken restaurants in the world. That's a lot of drumsticks.
Kenner's first Easy-Bake Oven in 1963 used an ordinary light bulb as its heat source. Talk about a bright idea.
The first American doughnuts were little "nuts" of dough that the Pilgrims brought from Holland. The holes came much later.
Stephanie and Adrienne Vendetti, founders of the website How to be a Redhead, created it to help redheads love their hair. Compliment a redhead today.
Men who usually don't cook make dinner, while everyone who normally cooks has to stay out of the kitchen unless there's an emergency. Dinner is served, eventually.
It began after Bank of America announced a $5 monthly debit card fee in 2011, and about 40,000 people joined credit unions that first day. Five bucks can start a movement.
James Naismith nailed peach baskets ten feet high in a YMCA gym, and the first game used a soccer ball. Nothing but peach.
Sal and Margarita Manriquez started selling ballpark nachos at the State Fair in Dallas in 1964. Cheese has been flying ever since.
Adolphe Sax, a Belgian instrument maker, invented the saxophone, and the first ones were designed for military bands. Smooth jazz started somewhere.
It asks what three things you'd bring if you were stranded somewhere with no way home. Snacks. Always bring snacks.

The teddy bear exists because a 1902 cartoon showed President Theodore Roosevelt refusing to shoot a bear, which inspired a New York couple to make "Teddy's bear." Best hunting trip ever for toy stores.
It marks 1973, when New Jersey became the first state to allow girls to play Little League baseball. Play ball, everybody.
The word "notary" comes from a shorthand that Cicero's clerk invented to take down Cicero's speeches. The original stamp of approval.
Puns show up in Sumerian cuneiform and Egyptian and Mayan hieroglyphics, so the groaning is thousands of years old. Those groans are ancient history.
The suggested celebration is reading Dr. Seuss books like Fox in Socks, which are full of tongue twisters. Say it three times fast.
Cappuccino is named for the Capuchin friars, whose reddish-brown hooded robes matched the color of the drink. Coffee with a hood.
The pupusa is El Salvador's national dish, a thick handmade tortilla stuffed with cheese, beans or pork and served with cabbage relish. Hard to beat a stuffed tortilla.
A pianist from Belarus named Ivan Manko created it in 2014. It hits all the right keys.
